title: Disentangling the percepts of illusory movement and sensory stimulation during tendon vibration in the EEG
description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from twenty healthy right-handed adults exposed to tendon vibration applied to the left elbow. Vibration of the biceps and triceps tendons at different frequencies either elicited an illusion of elbow extension or produced vibration sensation only (control). The data allow the neural correlates of illusory movement to be separated from those of sensory stimulation, using 16 electrodes over sensorimotor cortex.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a g.tec Nautilus wireless amplifier using 16 sensorimotor electrodes (10-10 system) at 500 Hz, with a 0.1-100 Hz hardware bandpass and a right earlobe reference. Electromechanical vibrators (Vibramoov) were placed on the distal biceps and triceps tendons of the left arm. Illusion trials used 90 Hz (biceps) and 50 Hz (triceps), and control trials used 70 Hz on both tendons. Each 3 s stimulation had a 1 s ramp-up, 1 s plateau and 1 s ramp-down. Each participant completed three blocks of 72 randomized vibrations (36 illusion, 36 control), with inter-stimulus intervals of 1-3 s.
